answers.text: The server looks up the pair (device id, change id) in applied_changes, not the change id alone. The device id is a random id the phone makes once on install and sends with every upload. Auth is out of scope, so the server trusts the id as sent. Changed the diagram, the server state section and the failure table to say so.

Until a download is applied, N shows the local edit B at version 5. Phone B's upload of B is a conflict, so B is saved on the server as N2. The page with seq 101 and seq 102 applies in one local transaction: N becomes A2 at version 6 and N2 is added together. The user sees B leave N and appear as N2 at that download. Nothing is lost, because B's outbox row is deleted only after the conflict result, and B is on the server by then.

Local B is replaced by A2 when seq 101 is applied, because version 6 is higher than the local version 5. This is safe because B is saved as N2 on the server, and in the diagram N2 arrives in the same page. The rule now says so explicitly, including the case where the row is still pending: the row keeps its own body and base, and its later upload conflicts.

Neither a source-device check nor a lookup is used. The accept response sets Phone A's local version to 6, so seq 101 at version 6 is not higher and is a no-op. Changed the upload and download rules and the diagram.

queued means the row waits for the next upload. sending means a batch has taken the row and is uploading it. A row moves to sending when a batch takes it, and is deleted when its result arrives. Only the start of the next sync moves it back: only one sync runs at a time, so a sending row seen at the start was cut off by a crash or drop, and it becomes queued again. Added this rule to the upload rules and to the failure table.

The server stops at the failing change and returns the results for the changes before it, plus the error. So the phone does get partial results. Earlier changes are committed and stay committed. The failed change was not committed. Later changes are not processed and stay queued. The upload ends that sync run. Added this rule and a failure row.

The server creates N2 and gives it a new id. A change carries no title, so the title is the server's current title for N plus " (conflict)". The conflict result includes N2's id, so the phone knows the id at once. The phone gets N2's content only from the download, which stays the only path that writes server notes into the local database.

The brief does not say whether title edits sync. This design carries only the body in a change, so title edits are not synced. The conflict title uses the server's current title, which is the only title the design has. Added as an open point, not decided here.

questions.text: When does the phone decide a sync should start, and what exactly does it send in a batch: which outbox rows, in what order, and with what fields besides change id, base and body?

questions.text: If phone A edited N again after Edit 2 was sent but before the result arrived, what is local N's version and body after the accepted result, and does the local body get overwritten?
questions.about: PA: Set local N version to 6, delete outbox row cA

answers.text: A sync starts when the connection returns, when the app comes to the foreground, and every 60 seconds while online. The brief sets these triggers. A batch takes up to 100 waiting rows (queued or sent), oldest first, and sends each row's change id, note id, base version and full body. The device id is sent once per request. Batches repeat until no rows wait, then the download runs. Added these to the upload rules.

The change id is kept from Edit 1. A row has one change id for its life, and Edit 2 only updates the body. You found a real bug in the old text. If the row was sent, the response was lost, and the row was then queued again, a new edit collapsing into it would send a new body under the old change id. The server would return the stored result for the old body, and the new body would be silently dropped. Fixed: a row gets a `sent` state once it has been sent. Edits collapse only into a `queued` row, which has never been sent. An edit to a sent or sending row starts a new row.

The phone marks rows with no result as sent, and the next sync sends them again, so a server error is retried at the next sync run. Nothing in this design stops the retry. A change that always fails is sent on every sync. The design has no backoff, no give-up rule and no message to the user, and the brief does not ask for them. I do not know which server errors are transient. Added as an open point.

Until a download applies, N shows the local body B at version 5. The user can keep editing N. Each edit saves locally, and a later upload conflicts because the server is past version 5, so the edit is saved as a conflict note. Nothing is lost, but while downloads keep failing, each edit burst can add another conflict note. The time the user can see the stale state is as long as downloads fail. There is no timeout. Added one line to the download rules that says this.

The sending row's base and the last applied version are both 5 here, because nothing applies while an upload is running. The new row uses the last applied version because the accept result is not known yet. If the phone guessed the result (version 6) and the change failed, the guess would be wrong. The base 5 is the safe choice: the new row cannot be accepted over the device's own change without a conflict. Walkthrough: cA (body A2, base 5) is sent. The user types A3, which becomes cB (base 5). cA is accepted as version 6. Local N keeps body A3 at version 5, because cB is still pending, so the version is not set. The next download brings A2 at version 6, so N shows A2. cB then conflicts and is saved as N2 with body A3. The user ends up with N at A2 and N2 at A3. Nothing is lost. The old text had a divergence bug here, fixed under Q16.

The phone does not know from the page alone. The rule is that it keeps requesting the next page in the same run until a page has fewer than 500 entries. Each page is applied in one transaction, and its cursor is saved in that transaction. Added to the download rules. A page of exactly 500 causes one more request that returns an empty page.

Nothing in the old text stopped two transactions from reading version 5 at once. Fixed: the server locks the note row while it checks the base and writes. The second change waits, then reads version 6 and becomes a conflict. A conditional update (write only where version equals the base, and check the row count) would also work. Added the lock to the upload rules and a row to the failure table.

The accepted result changes only the local version and the outbox row. It never touches the body. The old text would have set the version to 6 while the local body held the newer edit A3. Download would then never replace it, because 6 is not higher than 6. Local N would stay at A3 while the server holds A2. Fixed: the version is set to 6 only when no other row for the note is pending. Here the version stays at 5. The download then brings A2 at version 6, and the A3 row conflicts and is saved as N2. Local N and the server now agree, and nothing is lost. Also updated the diagram label.

questions.text: In the diagram, Phone B's first download attempt drops, then it retries. The rules say a dropped download ends the run. Does the retry happen in the same sync run, or at the next trigger (60 s timer etc.)? Which does the diagram show?
questions.about: PB: Download step again: entries after cursor 100

questions.text: After the conflict result, Phone B deletes the outbox row cB and its local N still shows body B at version 5. What marks N2 as the place B went to? Does the phone use the N2 id from the conflict result for anything, or is it only informational?
questions.about: API-->>PB: Conflict, N2 id, body B saved as N2

questions.text: The server lock on note N is held during the check and write. How does the server treat a change for a note id it has never seen, or a first-ever note created on a phone? Where does a new note get its server version and who creates it?
questions.about: Server: notes / Lock N, read current version

questions.text: The upload response for a batch returns a result per change. What does the phone do when a result is a conflict but a later row in the same batch is for the same note N? Is that later row based on a version that is now stale?
questions.about: Upload rules: A batch holds up to 100 waiting rows

questions.text: What does the download return when a phone first installs or has cursor 0? Does it get every entry in change_log, and how does it get the title of each note, since change_log rows carry only the full body?
questions.about: change_log: append-only rows / Download step

questions.text: When the phone applies an entry with a note id it has no local row for (like N2), where does the title come from, and what version does it store?
questions.about: PB: Apply both in one local transaction: N2 is added

answers.text: The retry does not happen in the same run. The rules say a dropped download ends the run and the cursor stays put, so the next run (the 60 s timer, reconnect or foreground) retries, starting with the upload step. The diagram showed an immediate retry, which was wrong. Fixed the diagram to show the run ending and the next run starting.

Nothing on the phone marks N2 as the place B went. The conflict result's N2 id is informational only: the phone does not store it. Phone B's local N keeps body B at version 5 until the download, and the download creates N2 with its title and body. The download is the only path that writes server notes into the local database, as in A7. Added this to the upload rules.

The design has no path that creates a note on a phone, and the brief covers only edits to existing notes. I do not know what the server should do with a change for a note id it has never seen, or who assigns a first version to a new note. A reasonable guess would be a server error, which retries on every sync, but that is not decided here. Added as an open point.

No extra rule is needed. The server checks each change in its own transaction, in batch order, and each check reads the version left by the changes before it. If the earlier change for N was accepted, the version moved and the later row (base 5) conflicts. If the earlier one conflicted, N's version did not move, so the later row's base decides it. The later row is based on the version the phone last applied, so it is stale only when N has moved, and then it conflicts as it should. Added one rule line to the upload rules that says this.

A download with cursor 0 returns every change_log entry from seq 1, in pages of 500, so a fresh install gets every log entry. The title was missing: the change_log rows carried only the body, so a download could not give a title for a new note such as N2. Fixed by adding the note's title to each change_log row, written at the same time as the version. Download rules now say a fresh install reads from seq 1, and that the retention open point covers a log that has been trimmed.

The title and version come from the entry. Each entry now carries the note's title, body and version, and the phone creates a local row with those values when it has none. N2 is stored with title 'Title (conflict)' and version 1. The phone does not choose a version itself. Fixed the change_log state, the download rules, and the diagram's download page and apply step.

questions.text: Phone B uploads cB and gets a conflict. The retry download then shows N becoming A2 and N2 appearing. But if phone B's download keeps failing, the user keeps editing N and each edit conflicts. Which version does each of those new rows use as its base, and does the phone ever learn the server is at 6 before it downloads?
questions.about: Download rules: Until a page is applied, the phone shows its local copy

questions.text: When the server returns a server error and stops, how does the phone tell a server error from a lost response or a dropped connection? What exactly does the phone do with the results it did get before the error?
questions.about: Upload rules: If a change fails with a server error

questions.text: For the lost-response retry on Phone A, the row is marked `sent` and goes out in the next sync. Where in the diagram does the retry happen (same run or next run), and does the download in between matter? What does Phone A show for N if the user edits again during that time?
questions.about: alt Phone A's upload response is lost in transit

questions.text: The server stores a result in applied_changes. For a retried change that was already a conflict, what does the phone get back, and does it create a second N2? Is the stored result the original N2 id?
questions.about: applied_changes: keyed by (device id, change id), storing the result

questions.text: In the diagram, Phone A's local N is at version 6 after the accept and the download is a no-op. How does Phone A learn seq 102 (N2), and does the cursor jump from 101 to 102 on its next download?
questions.about: sync_cursor: the last change log sequence number this phone has applied

questions.text: When the download page contains several entries for the same note (for example seq 101 and a later seq 105 for N), in what order does the phone apply them, and does it matter that the version check is the only guard?
questions.about: Download rules: Applying an entry is idempotent

answers.text: The new row's base is the last version the phone applied, which is 5 here, because the failed download means no newer version is known. The phone does not learn that the server is at 6 until an accept result for its own change or a download. A conflict result does not carry the server version. Each such row conflicts when uploaded and is saved as a conflict note. Added these lines to the download rules.

The batch response gives one result per change processed, in batch order. Each result is accepted, conflict, or error. A server error arrives as an error result for the failing change, so the phone can tell it from a lost response: a dropped or cut response gives no result at all. The phone applies the accepted and conflict results it received before the error, deletes those rows, and marks the error change and the later rows sent. Rows with no result are sent again at the next sync. Added this to the upload rules.

The retry happens in the next sync run, not the same one. A failed upload ends the run, so no download runs in between. The row stays sending, becomes sent at the start of the next run, and the upload step runs first. Meanwhile Phone A shows local body A2 at version 5. If the user edits again, the new row is queued with base 5 and shows in the UI. In the next run, the sent row cA goes first, is accepted at version 6 with its stored result, and the version stays 5 because cB is pending. The download then brings A2 at version 6, and cB conflicts and is saved as N2 with body A3. Diagram moved so the lost-response branch is an alt in the upload step, and the failure table says the run ends.

The phone gets back the stored result: the same conflict with the original N2 id. The server writes nothing on the retry, so no second N2 is created. The phone still does not store the id and gets N2 only through the download. Added this to the upload rules.

The diagram's download on Phone A returns only seq 101, because N2 did not exist yet. Phone A's cursor moves to 101. On its next download, seq 102 (N2) comes back and the cursor moves to 102. The cursor jump is normal, because it moves to the last seq applied. Added a note to the diagram.

The phone applies entries in seq order within the page. The version check alone is enough to decide each entry, because each note's version only goes up with its accepted writes. An older entry is never higher than a newer one already applied, so the result is the newest version whatever order the entries arrive in. Added this to the idempotence rule.

questions.text: The server-error result applies to a change that fails. Phone B's retry of a conflict: the stored result has N2's id, but what does the phone do if the stored result is an accepted result and the phone has since made a newer edit that is pending? Is the version still left unchanged?
questions.about: Upload rules: The phone deletes an outbox row only after receiving that change's result

questions.text: A row goes `sending` then `sent`. When a `sent` row is later sent and some other queued row for the same note is also in the batch, which goes first and how does the server see them? Do both rows carry base 5?
questions.about: Upload rules: An upload batch takes up to 100 waiting rows, oldest first

questions.text: When Phone B gets a conflict, it deletes row cB and N still shows B at version 5. If the user then edits N again before the download, what base does that new row get, and what does the user see after the download for N, N2 and the new edit?
questions.about: Download rules: Until a page is applied, the phone shows its local copy

questions.text: In the diagram Phone A's next run after the lost response: the retry returns the stored result from applied_changes. Does the server still re-check the base for this retry, or return the stored result before looking at version or locking N?
questions.about: Phone A's upload response is lost in transit / Look up (device A, cA) finds it already applied

questions.text: How does a failed upload (for example the network is simply offline when a sync starts) differ from the lost-response case in what the phone does, and when does the sync give up the run versus retry within it?
questions.about: Failure and retry: Connection drops before the upload reaches the server

answers.text: The stored result for a retry is returned as it was. An accepted result sets the local version only when no other row for that note is pending. With a newer row pending, the version stays where it was (5 in the example). The body is never changed. The download later brings the server body and version 6, and the pending row then conflicts. This is now stated in step 4.

The batch takes waiting rows oldest first, by creation time. The sent row cA was created earlier, so one request carries cA and then cB. The server checks them in batch order. Both carry base 5 here, because nothing has been applied since the row was made. If cA is accepted (or its stored accepted result is returned), the version is 6 and cB conflicts. If cA conflicts, N's version did not move, so cB's base decides. This is now stated in step 3.

After the conflict, the user's new edit C is saved to notes and to a new queued row with base 5, the last applied version. The download then sets N to A2 at version 6. The row keeps body C and is not applied to N. N2 (body B) arrives in the same page. The user sees A2 in N while C waits. When cC uploads, it conflicts because the server is at 6, and it is saved as a conflict note with body C. The end state is N at A2, N2 at B and the conflict note at C. Nothing is lost. Whether the UI should keep showing the pending C is left open in the open questions.

The server looks up (device id, change id) in applied_changes first, before it reads the version or locks N. If the change is found, it returns the stored result and writes nothing. It does not re-check the base on a retry. Only a change not found in applied_changes goes through the base check and the lock. This is now step 3a.

A request that fails before the upload reaches the server and a lost response both leave the rows sending. The phone handles both the same way: it ends the run, runs no download, and retries at the next run with the same change id. The phone cannot tell them apart. The server can, because it either has an applied record or does not. Within a run, the phone never retries. A failed upload or download request ends the run. A run goes on only after a successful batch or a successful page. The next trigger is the 60 s timer, a reconnect or the app coming to the foreground. This is now step 2.

teachbacks.text:
1. Edit (phone A, offline). The user edits note N, which both phones hold at version 5. The phone writes the new body into its local `notes` table and shows it straight away, with no network wait. It then updates the `outbox`. N has no row yet, so edit 1 adds a `queued` row (change id cA, note N, base 5, full body). Edit 2 finds that `queued` row and only changes its body, so cA keeps its change id and base 5 and now holds body A2. If a row for the note were `sending` or `sent`, a new `queued` row would be added instead, because a sent change may already be on the server. Nothing can fail here.

2. Edit (phone B, offline). Phone B does the same with one edit. It saves body B to its local `notes` and adds outbox row cB (base 5).

3. Sync run starts on phone A. Triggers are the connection returning, the app coming to the foreground, or a 60-second timer while online. The single-flight lock lets only one run go, and a trigger during a run does nothing. At the start of the run, any `sending` rows become `sent`. Then the run uploads first and downloads second.

4. Upload batch from A. The phone takes up to 100 waiting rows (`queued` or `sent`), oldest first, and marks them `sending`. One request carries the device id once. It also carries, for each row, the change id, note id, base version and full body. Here that is cA with base 5 and body A2.

5. Server handles cA, each change in its own transaction. First it looks up (device A, cA) in `applied_changes`. This check comes before any lock or base check. It finds nothing, so it locks note N and reads N's version, which is 5. That equals the base, so the change is accepted. In one transaction the server writes N at version 6, appends change_log seq 101 (note, title, version, full body, device, change id), and records the accepted result in `applied_changes` for (A, cA). Then it commits. The lock stops two changes to one note from running at once.

6. Failure branch, response lost. If the response never reaches the phone, the server has already committed everything. Row cA stays `sending`, the run ends, and there is no download. The next run turns the row into `sent` and uploads first. It retries cA with the same change id. The server finds (A, cA) in `applied_changes` and returns the stored result (accepted, version 6). It writes nothing, so there is no second write. If the request had never reached the server, the retry would just be the first apply. A server crash mid-change rolls the whole change back, so the retry behaves like a first attempt.

7. Phone A applies the result. The result is accepted, version 6. No other row for N is pending, so the phone sets its local N version to 6. It does not touch the local body. It deletes row cA. If another row for N were pending, the version would stay at 5, and that row's later upload would conflict.

8. Download on phone A. After a successful upload the phone asks for change_log entries after its cursor (100), up to 500 per page. The reply holds seq 101 (N, version 6, body A2). In one local transaction the phone applies entries in seq order. Entry 101 has version 6, which is not higher than the local 6, so it is a no-op. The cursor moves to 101 in the same transaction. The page has fewer than 500 entries, so the run ends. A page of exactly 500 would trigger one more request.

9. Phone B syncs (later). B uploads (cB, base 5, body B). The server finds no record for (B, cB), locks N and reads version 6. The base 5 differs, so this is a conflict. The server does not merge text. In one transaction it creates note N2 with a new id, titled N's current server title plus "(conflict)", with body B at version 1. It appends N2 to the change_log as seq 102 with its title. It records the conflict result, including N2's id, for (B, cB), and commits. A retry of this change would return the same stored result with the same N2 id, and would not create a second N2.

10. Phone B applies the conflict result. Body B is safe on the server as N2, so the phone deletes row cB. It does not store N2's id. Local N still shows body B at version 5. N2 will arrive only through a download.

11. Download on B, first attempt fails. B asks for entries after cursor 100. The connection drops mid-page, so the run ends. The cursor stays at 100, and nothing is partly applied because a page is applied in one transaction.

12. Next run on B. A trigger (60 s timer, reconnect or foreground) starts a new run. No rows are waiting, so only the download runs. It asks for entries after cursor 100 again and gets seq 101 (N, version 6, body A2) and seq 102 (N2, title, version 1, body B). In one transaction, entry 101 has version 6, higher than local 5, so N's body and version are replaced with A2 at version 6. Entry 102 is for a note the phone has no row for, so it creates N2 with that title, body and version. The cursor moves to 102. Both phones end up with N = A2 and a conflict copy N2 = B.

13. Other failures and rules.
- Server error on one change in a batch: the server stops there and returns earlier results plus the error. Earlier changes stay committed. The phone applies the earlier results and deletes those rows. The error row and later rows stay `sending`, then become `sent` and are retried next run.
- App killed during apply: the cursor and notes commit together or not at all, so the page is re-downloaded.
- Any failed request ends the run without a retry inside it. The next trigger starts a new run.
- A download entry with a higher version replaces the local body even when a pending row exists. That row's upload will then conflict and be saved as a conflict note.
- While downloads keep failing, each edit burst can add another conflict note, and there is no timeout.
gaps: How a note is first created on a phone, and what the server does with a change for a note id it has never seen. The document lists this as an open question, so I cannot explain a new note's first upload.
Where the first version of a new note comes from and who assigns it. The document lists this as an open question.
Whether the server error for an unknown note retries on every sync. The document says this 'is not decided'.
What happens to a change that keeps failing with a server error. There is no backoff, no give-up rule and no user message, and it is not known which errors are transient.
How title edits sync. A change carries only the body, so I cannot trace a title edit.

What a phone does if it has been offline longer than the change log is kept. The document says a full snapshot download is not designed, and it does not say what a fresh install does once the log has been trimmed.
Whether the UI keeps showing a pending edit after a download replaces the shown body. This is undecided.
How the server error is represented, and what the phone shows or does beyond retrying. The document does not say what kinds of errors exist.
